base.description: The bracket as FS ships DINRAIL4U, assembled, with its rail.

description: 4U 19in adjustable DIN rail bracket, FS DINRAIL4U: two black steel side brackets 360 mm deep whose front ends fold out into ears, joined by a rail panel carrying a 400 mm TS35 DIN rail that slides back along slots in the brackets, so DIN-rail equipment - industrial switches, media converters, power supplies, breakers - can stand in a 19in rack.

gaps.note: no FS document states what the DINRAIL4U or its rail may carry.
FS does not name the rail's profile; TS35 x 7.5 is read off the close-up render.

name: dinrail4u

chassis.note: 165.1 x 483.7 x 360 (HxWxD) over the ears, which is the part. THE EARS ARE BUILT IN: each is the front end of a side bracket folded out flat, one piece with the bracket that forms the frame's side (the datasheet's front and isometric views; renders g1 and g2 of SKU 376695), so under the owner's rule of 2026-10-09 they are part of the face and always drawn, 30.5 each side: the front is the 483.7 face, and the chassis is the 422.7 between the side brackets, which is what the other five faces and the side brackets in 3D are (as the FHD-1UFMT-N draws its plate). On the 300 dpi front view the outer edges stand 483.7 apart at 1.37 px/mm and the folds 30.5 in from each.

color.note: black steel and a silver zinc-plated rail, as every render shows.

eia.note: EIA-310 hole positions: the rail holes of each rack unit stand 6.35, 22.225 and 38.1 mm up from its bottom, and the two rails' holes are 465.1 mm apart across the rack. The part is taken as centred in the rack units it fills.

hosting.note: for #935: one TS35 x 7.5 rail, 400 mm long, centred 82.55 mm below the top of the 165.1 mm face, its panel's face 50.5 to 269.4 behind the ears; the width between the side brackets is 419.7; the space available behind the rail runs to the 360 mm depth. FS states no load rating. Recorded in `attrs.physical`.

joint.note: for #971: how the rail panel meets the side brackets. The panel (fs/dinrail4u-panel@2) is the 419.7 between the brackets' inner faces: the datasheet's 400.00 is the rail, and on its top view its plate runs from bracket to bracket (the top view p3 reuses is the DINRAIL2U's raster), the rail stopping short of each. At each end the panel folds back along the bracket's inner face as a flange, and a tab at its top and bottom lies on the bracket's edge, which is lowered 5.9 between the bracket's ends to take it (the side view, p3; gallery render g4 of SKU 376695). Two M5 screws a side (the quick start guide: "the M5 screws and nuts"; the side view draws two) pass through the bracket's two slots into the flange, which is how the panel slides and is fixed (#950). At the default setback the tab and flange run 159.9 to 196.1 behind the ears and the screws stand at 177.7, the offsets the setback note reads; the screws are common/pan-screw-m5@1, the pan head render g4 shows. The flange is drawn under the side bracket, seen through its slots and window; its depth is taken as the tab's. In the plan views the tab reaches 15.6 in from the bracket's inner face and overhangs its outer face by 8.9 (the top view, 1.116 mm a pixel); the overhang lies outside the plan views, which stop at the brackets, so only the 3D tab on the side views (standing 10.4 off the side, the plate's 1.5 and the overhang) carries it. The screw heads are drawn over the bracket, whole, on its outer face over the slot, as render g4 shows them (the bracket is `under` them), standing the plate's 1.5 off the face. WHAT IS ESTIMATED in this note, the rest being read from the drawings: the tab's 3.9 height on the side views, which no view dimensions (it is drawn to end on the lowered edge, inside the 5.9 step); the flange's depth along the bracket, taken as the tab's, and its height, taken as the whole span between the two tabs; the tab's 15.6 reach and 8.9 overhang, each about 14 and 8 pixels of a raster at 1.1 mm a pixel, so good to a millimetre or so at best, and here not the 4U's own, since its top view is the DINRAIL2U's raster reused; and the 5.9 of the lowered edge, 4.5 to 5 pixels of the side view's raster at 1.2 mm a pixel.

rail.note: a TS35 x 7.5 rail 400 long (fs/din-rail-ts35-400@1) centred on the panel's height, its centre line 82.55 below the top: the datasheet's front views draw it across the whole 400 panel at mid-height (the 4U's measures 82.2 down on the 300 dpi render, the 165.1 face's middle being 82.55).

rail-setback.note: the rail panel's front face can stand from 50.5 to 269.4 mm behind the ears, and is drawn at 159.9, the middle of that travel; the rail's face stands 7.5 in front of the panel's. The panel slides along the two long slots in each 360 mm side bracket ("the adjustable rails can be easily set back"; QSG: adjust the rail panel's position to suit the device). On the datasheet's side view (p3, an embedded 435 x 279 px raster, about 1.2 mm a pixel, read on a 600 dpi upsampled render at 3.258 px/mm along the 360) the slots run 65.7 to 289.8 and are about 5.2 wide, so a screw's centre travels from 68.3 to 287.2; the panel's tab spans 128.6 to 164.8 with its screw at 146.4, so the panel face stands 17.8 in front of the screw. The face travel is the screw travel less that. The gallery renders show it at both ends of that travel: g3 about 62 and g4 about 284 behind the ears, each read along the near side bracket as a fraction of its 360 (a three-quarter render, so to perhaps 10 per cent). With no single photographed position, the middle of the travel is the default. The travel is stated as the `rail-setback` adjustment, whose three stops are the two ends and that middle; the three din-rail-setback attrs restate it.

sheet.note: `shell: sheet`, 1.5: an open frame of bent steel - two side brackets, a rail panel and a rail - which a solid box would hide. In 3D the side brackets are built from the side views, standing their thickness off them. The panel is a well on the front view whose floor is the plate at its setback, black with its cut-outs open, and the rail stands 7.5 off that floor with its face art - flanges, crown, slots - on its front. The six views are elevations.
